raw_response:
The customer dimension is an SCD2 table: 30 customers have two rows, one with is_current=False and one with is_current=True. Joining on customer_id alone therefore duplicates transactions for those customers. This explains why gold_region_daily has more rows than silver_transactions. The reconciliation gap is 5251 − 4558 = 693, which is plausible for 30 customers out of 200 across all dates.

The fix is to keep only current rows in silver_customers. All 200 customers have exactly one is_current=True row, so the dimension becomes unique per customer_id.

There is a business question about whether to use the region as of each transaction date (a point-in-time join). The valid_from values are 2025-01-01 for current rows and 2023-06-01 for old rows. There is no valid_to column, but the old rows would have been valid from 2023-06 until 2025-01. All transactions fall in January 2026, so the current row applies to every transaction. Filtering to is_current is therefore correct.

Gold_customer_spend and the other gold tables are not affected. silver_customers keeps the same columns.
